reasoning: Round 2 rebuild on the supervisor's findings. (1) Margins restated on the company's segment adjusted EBITDA basis (round 1 mixed EBITA and EBITDA): Comms 12.3/12.5/12.9%, BS 20.5/19.5/19.0%; engine EBIT = that less segment depreciation. BS moves up from 19%/18.5% adj. EBITDA to 0.5pt under the CEO's ~20% center, held below it for labor-cost pressure (EC&M: 83% of electrical contractors short of labor), moratorium idling and normalising lead-time pricing (rule 0c). (2) Supplier finance added: 247 of the 524 program is debt-like, from my AP-stretch arithmetic on XBRL (pre-program AP 5.63% of revenue), close to the supervisor's 252.9; interest blended to 5.3%. (3) Kilian's shared dc_mor haircut applied to Building Systems on the non-hyperscaler share (1-0.62), mapped to DY's Feb-Jan quarters (FY2028 0.106, FY2029 0.0865). (4) Tax to the company-stated 26% non-GAAP rate. (5) Multiples repriced on one date: peers and DY at 2026-11-24 closes on consensus fetched 2026-11-25 (DY on an estimated post-print NTM 17.5) -> whole-company median 14.5x (was 16.0x at 11-02 prices; peers fell), DY 10.2x, k=0.8 exit 10.9x; EV/EBITDA 12.35x vs DY 8.07x -> 8.8x GAAP = 8.5x adjusted. (6) Communications rebuilt in dollars by program: FTTH -340 (AT&T capex cut, MasTec deferrals), wireless +150, copper +75, long-haul 550/900 (trimmed for ramp), BEAD in FY2029 (AlixPartners: BEAD money mostly in 2027, mid-mile round 2H27): Comms +3.9% FY2028, +7.2% FY2029, just below the CEO's mid-single digit then accelerating as he said. Net: research target (12m) $250 (from $257): the lower peer median (-), supplier finance and moratorium (-), higher BS and Comms margins on the corrected basis and higher tax netting out. I disagree with the set's 13.0x exit: a price move across the whole peer group is evidence of the multiple the market pays on one date, and the supervisor itself asked for one date. P10 $125 / P90 $399 move drivers (FTTH spread, long-haul pace, BS labor/moratorium, margins) plus 2.5-3 turns.

model_inputs.structure_note: Two-segment annual driver build (Communications = core FTTH/maintenance/wireless/copper/BEAD + long-haul/DCI; Building Systems = data-center electrical + structured cabling, less the shared dc_mor moratorium haircut on the non-hyperscaler share), FY2027-FY2029 (FY ends late January). Margin drivers are segment ADJUSTED EBITDA (company basis; segments sum to consolidated adjusted EBITDA); engine EBIT = that less segment depreciation (Comms 3.1%, BS 1.0%), before amortization of acquired intangibles; SBC deducted by the engine (cost). Value carried by a P/E horizon leg (0.75) on the build's own NTM adjusted EPS (ex amortization, SBC costed) and an EV/EBITDA cross-check (0.25) on NTM EBITDA after SBC (GAAP-like, peers' basis). Net debt includes the debt-like part of the supplier-finance program (247). No DCF (engine policy). Leg weights are judgment, untested.
model_inputs.gap_note: Annual (not quarterly) set, built by a forecaster for comparison. Long-haul base split is an estimate (low confidence). DY's Nasdaq/Zacks feed is still pre-print on 2026-11-25; the own NTM P/E uses an estimated post-print vintage (17.5) so DY and peers sit on one date and vintage. dc_mor: I map the shared monthly values to DY's Feb-Jan fiscal quarters (FY2028 mean 0.106, FY2029 0.0865); the round-1 supervisor list looks one quarter shifted - for Kilian to confirm. Supplier finance: 247 debt-like (my AP-stretch arithmetic) vs supervisor 252.9 (18.4 days); all 524 would be about -3%. Engine charges 5.3% on the whole net debt incl. the non-interest-bearing supplier finance part (blended rate). Other non-operating expense (~$10M/yr) not in engine EPS (about -$0.25/share). Judgment calls: BS margin 19.5% vs CEO center 20% (about -1.5%); Comms FY2028 +3.9% vs the CEO's mid-single digit (about -2%); exit P/E at 2026-11-24 prices (10.9x) vs the set's 13.0x on 2026-11-02 prices (that card).
